description:
Each lease is one record changed by one lock-load-change-publish sequence, and claims decide their event from the issue record, so no lease or claim operation reads the claims log or the event log's records.

## Background

The claims control plane kept every lease in one index that was a second authority beside a replayed log, repeated its lock and publish steps in each operation, and kept test-only APIs. The claim command parsed the whole event log to decide its event. This story stores one record per lease, runs every lease operation through one held lease lock, addresses every lease command by issue, and makes a claim's event follow the assignee.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Reading or changing one issue's lease reads only that issue's lease record, and no lease operation reads the claims log.
- [hard] REQ-02: An interrupted lease operation leaves the prior or the next lease, and nothing rebuilds lease state from the log.
- [hard] REQ-03: A claim appends its event exactly when the assignee changes and parses no event-log record.
- [hard] REQ-04: This checkout's leases are carried into lease records, and the lease docs describe them.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Leases are per-issue records under one lease sequence
